description: Compare the distribution of one categorical column between two datasets. Reports a category that appeared - which a consumer switching exhaustively on the column has no branch for - a category that vanished, and shares that moved beyond a tolerance. Shares are proportions of all rows including empty ones, so a rising empty rate is visible rather than hidden by renormalisation. Pay 140000 atomic USDC on Base via exact x402. MCP does not pay; it provides a challenge handoff.

after.description: The later dataset. Delimited text with a header row, at most 262144 bytes and 5000 data rows. RFC 4180 quoting is honoured. Nothing is fetched.
after.example:
status
open
closed
closed
closed
disputed
disputed

before.description: The earlier dataset. Delimited text with a header row, at most 262144 bytes and 5000 data rows. RFC 4180 quoting is honoured. Nothing is fetched.
before.example:
status
open
open
open
closed
closed
legacy

delimiter.description: Single field separator. Defaults to a comma.

share_tolerance.description: Absolute movement in share that is acceptable. Defaults to 0.05.

name: categorical_distribution_drift

categories.description: Every category with its counts, shares and share change, ordered by how much it moved.

complete.description: Whether everything supplied was examined. False means part of the data was not, which is a different problem from data that is wrong.

finding_count.description: The true total, even when the listing is bounded.

row.description: 1-based and counting the header, so it matches a text editor.

passed.description: The same verdict under the name shared across the caller-supplied families.

request_id.description: Delivery request identifier; also returned in x-foundry-request-id.

stable.description: True only when both datasets were fully read, no category appeared or vanished, and no share moved beyond tolerance.

title: Categorical Distribution Drift
